name: Finite-bandwidth sensitivity to bare-frequency versus hopping disorder
origin: Meier2025 published Methods p.9 explicit expectation; chiral-symmetry discrimination is our inference.
minimal_model: Use the Meier XY/cavity single-excitation hopping chain, not a mislabeled random-exchange Heisenberg chain. Launch the same normalized pi/2 Gaussian, optionally compare q0=0.7.
controlled_comparison: Same length, initial support/width, propagation time or distance, disorder region, random seed ensemble, and a stated matched perturbation-energy budget. Compare zero disorder, random hopping only, random onsite frequencies only; optional third physical Heisenberg-exchange case with correlated diagonal and hopping disorder.
null: At the chosen finite packet bandwidth and distance, the two error types reduce transport comparably.
discriminating_result: A reproducible finite-bandwidth/distance regime where symmetry-breaking onsite noise causes a qualitatively or quantitatively different degradation, not explained by mismatched perturbation normalization.
failure_criterion: No held-out ensemble separation after fair normalization and size/time convergence; then retain as a negative result rather than infer symmetry protection.
limits: The bare-frequency benchmark is untested in Meier, but disorder-class differences are known. It does not prove a new clock scaling or reproduce the full open clock.

name: Launch-state encoding under incomplete Hamiltonian calibration
origin: Haselgrove2005 explicit Conclusion; a modern constrained benchmark, not generic new robust control.
minimal_model: One-excitation open chain with fixed sender window A, receiver B, arrival time T. M_delta=P_B exp(-i H_delta T) P_A.
baselines: Nominal SVD right singular vector of M_0
Ensemble encoding: top eigenvector of mean(M_delta^dagger M_delta)
null: Nominal SVD is already sufficiently robust; ensemble training gives no reproducible improvement.
failure_criterion: No improvement on an independent disorder/calibration-error ensemble, or advantage disappears with equal support and fixed T.
limits: This tests static Hamiltonian uncertainty only. It does not test total-spin nonconservation, finite-temperature dynamics, detector efficiency, or environmental decoherence.
